findings.text: Upheld as an advisory. PUSH_REMOTE and PUSH_ORIGIN are environment overrides that exist only for the test, and no criterion asked for them (Q5). The test could inject remote and origin through commitAndPush instead.

Upheld as an advisory. passingFacts, together with plan.ts:91-115 overwriting one placeholder at a time, ties plan.ts's read order to decidePlan's internal refusal order, so a new refusal means editing three places (Q5). It is still one job, so the reviewer rates it advisory.
Upheld as an advisory. The initial hold repeats decideHold's free value and needs a cast to do it (Q2, boilerplate).
Upheld as an advisory. The name resolveBinary hides its main side effect, which is staging a copy of the running binary into the data directory (Q3, naming).
Upheld as an advisory. The hold's summary line is written '<previous> speaks <m>' here but '… speaks <n>' in the table at line 438. release-docs.test.ts checks only the table (Q11).

Lowered from defect to advisory. The finding names spec.md:266, which is outside the diff (spec.md is not in review/files.txt). Only for the risk gate does a line of the item's own spec count as inside the change, so this cannot be upheld as a defect here. On the substance (Q4): a test could check that the ADR contains the strings D-1 to D-5, --force and 0008, but that would only show the strings are present. AC-76 asks that the ADR records the decisions, the alternatives and the limits, and that is prose a reviewer reads. docs/adr/0029-release-distribution.md:3, 21, 31-35 and 57-59 do record D-1 to D-5, the --force limit and the supersession of ADR 0008's Homebrew row. Noted as a gap the author may close with a citation test like AC-78's.

Upheld as an advisory. The list of possible summary lines is typed out by hand, not derived from OUTCOMES in scripts/release/lib.ts:104. A new outcome kind missing from the runbook table would still pass. The test does fail today if a row is removed, so AC-78 has a test that fails on reversion (Q1 holds; Q6 is the weakness).

Upheld as an advisory. module.includes(flag) matches a flag anywhere in the command's source, comments and other strings included, so it checks less than the criterion's 'a flag its module names' (Q5).

Dropped, named here as an advisory. The probe at .crew/work/2026-11-12-004-the-release-publishes-everywhere-by-itse/probes/generated-files-held.md shows that tests/integration/plugin-script.test.ts:94-101 holds every generated file (plugins/opencode/binary.js and the shipped wizardingcode-mem.sh copies) equal to what scripts/plugins.ts generates from OLDER_JS and the template, and that the test passes. The stale-copy path the finding describes is already covered, so the finding fails no question.

Upheld as an advisory. The unit test uses v99, not the v99.0.0 branch-tag scenario AC-65 names. The merged-only listing is held only through the stub in tests/integration/release-commands.test.ts:97, which does fail if the command changes. The criterion is covered, but its test does not read as the criterion (Q6).

Upheld as an advisory (hardening). The production command still honours the test overrides PUSH_REMOTE and PUSH_ORIGIN. Only someone who can change main could set them, and the extraheader is scoped to github.com. Ignoring the overrides when GITHUB_ACTIONS is set would close it.

Upheld as an advisory. The latest job holds packages: write without environment: release and is gated only by plan's check on refs/heads/main. ADR 0029's Limits already accept this. It records where the barrier sits, for piece 3.
Advisory, debt. Existing jobs use actions pinned by mutable major tags while holding contents: write and packages: write. These lines are not new in this diff.
Advisory, debt. The publish job's checkout keeps persisted credentials. The diff only added fetch-depth: 0 here, so this predates the change.

Upheld as an advisory. The distribute job dispatches distribute.yml and turns green at once, so a failed npm, tap or marketplace write may show only on the dispatched run's page. ADR 0029 states this limit and the runbook points to the 'distribute v<version>' run. Waiting on the run would make a failure visible on the release itself.

Upheld as an advisory. /GH006|protected branch/i does not match a ruleset's GH013 refusal, so the named repair at docs/runbooks/release.md:458 never shows. The push still fails visibly and can be repeated.

Upheld as an advisory. 'Dry run before the first real dispatch' is written in the runbook only, not in code. The way back is stated (spec.md:274, a higher version) and plan's environment refusal stops the tag's automatic run. The sentence 'The first tag after this setup exists…' contradicts itself and should say 'the first tag that carries this item'.
Advisory, debt. release.yml's existing jobs pin actions by tag while distribute.yml pins by commit. This predates the diff.

Upheld as an advisory. ADR 0029 supersedes ADR 0008's Homebrew row and amends its npm and curl rows, but ADR 0008 still says 'Status: accepted' with no pointer forward. The repository's convention (ADR 0004) is a status line on the older ADR (Q6). The fix is one sentence on 0008's status line.

Upheld as an advisory. The npm version check is inline bun -e code calling Bun.semver.order, the only decision of the workflow outside scripts/release/lib.ts and outside a unit test. It crosses no boundary (Q6).
Advisory, debt. The table still names the retired shibaox paths and repositories. It is a historical record written before ADR 0011 and was not caused by this diff.

Upheld as an advisory. plan accepts any complete, non-draft release for the tag without checking that the tag's release.yml run succeeded, so a manual dispatch could distribute a release finished by hand (Q1). The gates run first on the tag path, and ADR 0029's Limits already state this.
Upheld as an advisory. setup-node asks for node-version: 24, a floating major, while every other tool in the file is pinned. The npm >= 11.5.1 check at line 97 protects trusted publishing (Q6).
Advisory, debt. The existing jobs pull actions by moving tag while holding write permissions. This predates the diff.
Advisory, debt. The workflow-level contents: write reaches the build job. The new distribute job narrows itself to actions: write, but its neighbours are unchanged.
